title: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” — Genesis 18:14
paragraphs: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” — Genesis 18:14
You laughed.

Not out loud.
But deep inside… you did.

Because what God promised feels impossible now.
Too late. Too broken. Too far gone.
Sarah laughed too.

Old. Barren. Worn by years of disappointment.
When God said she would carry a child, her heart whispered, “That ship has sailed.”
And heaven responded with one question:
“Is anything too hard for the LORD?”
Pause there.

Not “Is this difficult?”
Not “Does this make sense?”
But too hard.

We measure life by limits.
God moves in the realm of the impossible.
But here’s what we miss…

This verse is not just about a miracle birth.
It’s about a dead heart coming back to life.

Because the same God who opened Sarah’s womb…
would one day open a tomb.

Through Jesus Christ, death itself was confronted—
and defeated.

Your situation?
Your failure?
Your secret sin?
Not too hard.
The cross already proved it.

Sin looked permanent.
Shame looked final.
But grace said, “Watch Me.”
And resurrection answered.

So if you’re doubting today—
if your faith feels thin, your hope delayed—
Hear the voice of God again:
“Is anything too hard for Me?”

Not your past.
Not your addiction.
Not your broken story.
But there’s a turn…

God doesn’t just ask for belief.
He calls for surrender.

Because the greatest miracle
is not changed circumstances—
It’s a changed heart.

Repent.
Come back.
Trust the One who does what you cannot.
And watch impossibility bow to His name.

From doubt to promise.
From laughter to life.
